newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN SOUND WARNING TO ANDERLECHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-EKEREN SOUND WARNING TO ANDERLECHT.

text.p: At first sight, winning a record ninth Belgian Cup should be a simple task for Anderlecht.
The proud Brussels side can boast a record 24 league titles and have two European Cup Winners' Cups, one UEFA Cup and two European Super Cups under their belt.
They were beaten just twice in their previous 10 Belgian Cup finals, with the last loss dating back to 1977 when Ekeren, their opponents in the final, were still lingering in a low regional division.
But times have changed for lucky Ekeren, based in a town of 22,000 just north of the port of Antwerp.

With an average crowd of just 6,500, they are unlikely to become a soccer powerhouse but have been a welcome tonic to the Belgian league since landing in the first division eight years ago, producing unusually daring and dazzling play focused on attack.
In their short first division career, Ekeren reached the Cup final twice, in 1990 and 1995, but were mercilessly beaten both times by FC Liege and Club Brugge respectively.
They qualified for the UEFA Cup twice, in 1991 and 1996, but crashed out in the first round on both occasions.
The bare facts also suggest that Anderlecht remain clear favourites to win Sunday's final.

They have already secured a berth in next season's UEFA Cup -- making their 35th successive appearance on the European stage -- by beating relegation-doomed Mechelen 2-0 last Sunday and edging into fourth place in the final standings, 15 points behind new champions Lierse.
Ekeren by contrast ended 10th in the league, another 12 points adrift of Lierse, for which their erratic defence -- the third weakest in the 18-team division -- was to blame.
Both teams were almost equally prolific with Anderlecht scoring 59 times, Ekeren 56 times. But Ekeren had 57 goals against, Anderlecht just 36.
Despite the apparent flaws in defence, many believe it will be third time lucky for Ekeren.

Still in the danger zone in early April, Ekeren gradually got into their stride and pulled off their biggest upset earlier this month when they beat Anderlecht 4-1 after a hat-trick by mercurial Canadian international Tomasz Radzinski.
And while Anderlecht struggled to overcome Mechelen on Sunday, Ekeren had a party at home against neighbours Antwerp, beating them 6-3 after another Radzinski hat-trick.
The Cup history books also give Ekeren the edge.
They knocked out Anderlecht in the semifinals of the 1995 Cup after what the club's yearbook described as their best game ever.
Anderlecht had won the home leg 2-0 but Ekeren hit back in the return leg, winning it 4-0.
"We're in a winning mood. We're ready for the Cup final," Ekeren coach Herman Helleputte said.
